subject: Private endpoint egress & firewall clarifications — allowlist and control plane
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <security@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private runtime — firewall & allowlist requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re kicking off the network design for a Private deployment of Redwood (VPC connector) and need a definitive list of outbound IPs and firewall rules so our perimeter team can bind it into the change window. A few specifics from our side:

- We cannot open broad outbound egress; prefer an allowlist of CIDRs or SNI-based allowlist if you support it.
- TLS + SNI inspection is how we enforce destination allowlists — can Redwood guarantee stable SNI fingerprints for the control plane endpoints?
- We have to know which destinations are required for: control plane (auth, telemetry), model runtime traffic, and optional update check-ins.
- Any support for Mutual TLS or customer-managed proxying (so traffic originates from our NAT IPs) would be helpful.

Can you provide the list and a short example firewall snippet we can share with the ops team? Procurement also asked for SOC2 artifact references and a DocuSign link for the SLA — I’ve cc’d them here.

Thanks,
Jordan Miles
Security Architect — Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

Hi Jordan — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. I’ve pulled together the initial artifacts you asked for: we’re attaching a short runbook, a CSV of the static control-plane IPs, and a few firewall snippet examples. Quick summary upfront:

- Control plane: static IP ranges (listed in egress-ip-list.csv) used for auth, billing, and control-plane telemetry. These are stable across a monthly cadence and suitable for perimeter allowlisting.
- Runtime/model traffic: by default originates from our private runtime pool — we offer two modes: 
  1) Redwood-managed egress (ephemeral outbound from our runtime fleet) — recommended for simplest setup; requires allowlisting the runtime service FQDNs/SNI patterns rather than many IPs.
  2) Customer-managed egress (recommended for strict network controls) — traffic is routed through your proxy/NAT; we support configuring an outbound proxy for the runtime so traffic originates from your NAT IP.
- TLS/SNI: control-plane endpoints have stable SNI values; I’ve highlighted them in the runbook under section 2. If you prefer SNI-only enforcement, we can provide the exact hostnames to allow.
- mTLS: we do not require mutual TLS for runtime calls today; we offer mutual auth options for Private control plane communications if you enable the dedicated deployment package — Kimberly can share details.

Next steps we propose:
1) Review the attachments with your ops team and confirm whether you want Redwood-managed runtime egress or will terminate via your NAT/proxy.
2) If you need strict static egress for runtime, provide the customer NAT IPs and we’ll validate connectivity during the engineering window.
3) Procurement — I’ve included a DocuSign link in related links; please let us know any redlines.

I’ll leave the tech details to David/Kimberly for the firewall snippets.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private runtime — firewall & allowlist requirements

Marissa / Jordan — adding technical clarifications from the infra side. Key recommendations and the reasoning behind them:

1) Split the rules: control plane vs runtime.
   - Control plane (auth, telemetry, console): allowlist static CIDRs in egress-ip-list.csv (TCP 443). These IPs are stable for the month and are ideal for perimeter rules.
   - Runtime/model outbound: prefers SNI/FQDN allowlist if you cannot accept large CIDR lists. Runtime service uses these hostnames: runtime.redwood-inference.com, artifacts.redwood-inference.com, updates.redwood-inference.com

2) SNI fingerprinting: SNI is supported, but be aware middleboxes that terminate TLS for inspection may rewrite SNI. If your environment does TLS-inspection proxies, customer-managed proxying (so traffic originates from your NAT) is more reliable.

3) mTLS & client certs: we can enable mutual TLS for the control plane channel if you require it — that provides stronger binding than IP/SNI alone. For runtime traffic, mTLS is available on the Dedicated model; on standard Private we can discuss a short-term workaround (static allowlist + proxy).

4) Example firewall snippets (high-level):
   - Allow outbound TCP 443 to 52.14.103.0/24 (control-plane cluster-1)
   - Allow outbound TCP 443 to 34.95.210.0/24 (control-plane cluster-2)
   - Permit outbound to SNI runtime.redwood-inference.com (SNI match) for runtime requests

5) Operational notes:
   - We send periodic update-checks to updates.redwood-inference.com — if you block this, automated agent updates will pause.
   - For a complete audit package (ASN mapping, IP change cadence), we can provide a signed manifest as part of your onboarding.

If you confirm whether Acme will host the outbound proxy or prefer Redwood-managed egress, we’ll produce a final rule set and test plan for your change window.

-David
David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks David — this is helpful. A few clarifying answers from our side:

- We will not allow wide ephemeral ranges. We prefer two options (in priority):
  1) Customer-managed proxy/NAT (so all outbound originates from our static NAT IPs and you can accept those).
  2) SNI-based allowlist for the three hostnames you listed — but only if SNI is preserved end-to-end (we will not permit TLS-terminating proxies that change SNI).
- We can accept the control-plane static CIDRs for allowlisting. Please confirm the monthly cadence for IP churn and provide an email distribution list for IP change notices.
- Procurement: we need SOC2 artifact references and the SLA DocuSign. Also request confirmation that no runtime payloads are mirrored to 3rd-party telemetry services without customer opt-in.

Assuming we choose option 1 (proxy/NAT), next steps:
- We will provide NAT IPs by Mon 12/6 and would like a connectivity test window the week of 12/13.
- Please send a validation checklist for the change window (ports, DNS expectations, test curl examples).

Jordan
Jordan Miles
Security Architect — Acme Health
